evals.prompt: Create a professional Q4 business report as a Word doc — cover page, table of contents, executive summary, performance tables, and recommendations. I need a real .docx with proper headings, not just bold paragraphs.
evals.expected_output: A .docx with Title/Subtitle cover, field-backed TOC (w:fldChar TOC), Heading 1/2 styles (not Normal+bold), at least one table with Light Grid Accent 1 style and caption, 1.07 body line spacing, and footer Page X of Y. Passes validate_docx.py --strict.
expectations: Produces a .docx file
Uses Heading 1/2 named styles — no fake headings
Includes a field-backed TOC (w:instrText TOC), not typed text
Includes at least one styled table with a Caption paragraph
Has explicit page geometry (A4 or Letter) and header/footer page numbers
Passes scripts/validate_docx.py --strict

evals.prompt: I need a one-page resume as a Word doc — tight margins, contact header, experience bullets, and a skills matrix table. Must fit one page and open clean in Google Docs.
evals.expected_output: A Letter Resume Tight .docx (0.45/0.50in margins) with no header/footer, Title-centered name, tight List Bullet spacing (2pt), skills matrix table with Table Grid, and estimated page count 1. Passes --check-resume-length --max-pages 2.
expectations: Produces a .docx file
Uses 0.45/0.50in resume margins and no page numbers
Experience bullets use List Bullet style with tight spacing
Skills matrix is a styled table (not plain text)
Page count estimate <= 2
No filler or lorem ipsum

evals.prompt: Generate an invoice as a Word doc — seller/buyer blocks, line-item table with quantities and unit prices, totals row, and payment terms. The math must be right.
evals.expected_output: A .docx invoice with seller/buyer blocks, Light Shading Accent 1 line-item table (Qty × Unit Price = Amount per row), summary table with Total Due, right-aligned numeric columns, banded rows, and payment terms footer. Amounts compute correctly.
expectations: Produces a .docx file
Line-item table has correct column widths summing to content width
Numeric columns right-aligned, header fill accent
Totals row is distinct (bold/shaded)
Includes payment terms paragraph (not just a table)
Passes validate_docx.py --audit-styles

evals.prompt: Make a formal contract as a Word doc — title, parties, definitions, and multilevel numbered clauses (1., 1.1, 1.1.1). I need real multilevel numbering, not typed numbers.
evals.expected_output: A .docx with multilevel numId (w:abstractNum/w:num) producing 1. / 1.1 / 1.1.1 hierarchy, A4 with gutter, TOC field, evenAndOddHeaders setting, signature blocks as borderless tables. Numbering is field-backed, not typed.
expectations: Produces a .docx file
Uses a single numId with 3 levels — not typed 1.1.1 in Normal
Has w:abstractNum / w:num in word/numbering.xml
Includes TOC field and footer Page X of Y
Signature blocks are tables with lines, not underscore text
Passes validate_docx.py --check-fields

evals.prompt: Convert my report.docx to legacy .doc and also to PDF. I need both.
evals.expected_output: Canonical .docx plus derived .doc and .pdf via LibreOffice headless (soffice --headless --convert-to). Script logs conversion commands and never claims python-docx writes .doc natively. Both outputs have matching page count to source.
expectations: Writes .docx first as canonical output
Converts via soffice --headless --convert-to doc and pdf when requested
Logs conversion path explicitly (not silent .doc write)
Errors clearly if LibreOffice not on PATH
Delivers .docx alongside derived artifacts, not alone
